revision_history.description: System requirement authored because SYS.2 was recorded as a coverage gap with no system requirement record in either profile. System-level: it states what the integrated item must do and allocates to the existing technical requirements rather than restating them.

statement: The item shall publish its mode, its charge and discharge limits and its active fault condition to the vehicle control unit, and shall act on a state request from that unit only when the request is consistent with the item's own safety evaluation; where it is not, the item shall refuse the request and publish the refusal with its reason.
rationale: The system-level statement of the integration contract with the vehicle manufacturer. It resolves the tension named in the stakeholder need FB2-SYS-NED-000004 in one direction and states the direction explicitly, because a requirement that said only 'the item honours state requests' would leave the safety case resting on the item being overridden cleanly, and 'cleanly' is not a property any record here establishes. The publication half is separated from the refusal half deliberately: publication is a capability the vehicle manufacturer needs in every mode, and refusal is a safety behaviour that only exists when the item has already judged something unsafe.

acceptance_criteria.measure: Modes and active faults published in every mode
Charge and discharge limits published to the control unit
Requests contradicting the item's own evaluation that were acted on

safety_allocation.safety_goal_ref: N/A - the interface itself is not allocated an ASIL; its integrity is bounded by the cybersecurity requirements FB2-SAF-SEC-000003 and FB2-SAF-SEC-000004
safety_allocation.mitigation: Message-level integrity and freshness verification, and the explicit refusal path

limitations: Synthetic. This requirement describes a hypothetical programme and establishes nothing about the real foxBMS project.
